explain.1: Load PyTorch, so we can use torch.something.
explain.2: Load PyTorch's ready-made functions (softmax, cross_entropy) under the short name F.
explain.4: Our training text: the only thing your model will learn from.
explain.5: set() keeps each character once. sorted() puts them in order. This is the vocabulary.
explain.6: len() counts the characters in the vocabulary.
explain.7: An empty dictionary. It will hold pairs like 'h' → 3.
explain.8: Another empty dictionary, for the reverse: 3 → 'h'.
explain.9: enumerate() gives each character with its position: 0 and the 1st character, 1 and the 2nd, and so on.
explain.10: Save this pair in the dictionary: character → number.
explain.14: An empty list for every group's third-last letter.
explain.15: An empty list for every group's second-last letter.
explain.16: An empty list for every group's last letter.
explain.17: An empty list for every 'next character' (the right answers).
explain.18: Go through every 3-letter group in the text. Stop 3 early, so each group has a next letter.
explain.19: The group's third-last letter, as a number.
explain.22: The letter that really comes next: the right answer.
explain.23: Turn the list into a tensor, so PyTorch can use it.
explain.27: Show how many groups (examples) we have.
explain.30: Fix the random numbers, so you get the same result every time.
explain.31: Table 1: random scores for the third-last letter.
explain.32: Table 2: random scores for the second-last letter.
explain.33: Table 3: random scores for the last letter.
explain.37: How big a step to take each time we fix the scores.
explain.38: Train 300 times: predict, measure, find directions, move.
explain.39: a) Predict: for every group, add one row from each table.
explain.40: b) Measure: how wrong were the scores? A smaller loss is better.
explain.44: c) Find directions: PyTorch fills weights.grad with which way to move each score.
explain.45: d) Move: change every score in Table 1 a little, against its gradient.
explain.48: % is the remainder. This is true at steps 0, 50, 100, … so we print every 50 steps.
explain.49: Show the step number and the loss.
explain.52: Fix the random numbers, so you get the same result every time.
explain.53: Start writing from “the”: the model needs 3 letters to begin.
explain.54: Write 40 more characters, one per round.
explain.55: Add the rows for the last 3 letters written so far.
explain.56: Turn the added scores into chances.
explain.57: Spin the weighted wheel and take out the picked number.
explain.58: Add the picked letter to the text.
